overall_reason: The rows name real work ('Checkout redesign', 'Search speedup', 'Pricing copy') with branch, author and relative time ('main · Maya Chen', '12m ago').

score.reason: T-LABEL-READ and T-TERMS pass on literal labels; T-STATE-COPY fails because build state and failure are carried by icons, not words.

findings.evidence: The 'Pricing copy' row carries only a red circled-x icon and a time; the 'Search speedup' row carries only a spinner icon. No word on the card says 'Failed' or 'Building', or what to do next.
findings.before: "Pricing copy" with a status icon only
findings.after: A status word per row ('Live', 'Building', 'Failed') and, on the failed row, the next step (for example 'View log')
findings.why: A reader who cannot tell the icons apart learns nothing from the words about which deploy failed.

strengths: The project names and the 'main · Maya Chen' meta line carry specific facts.
The 'Deploy' button sits under the heading 'Recent deploys', so the verb's object is clear.
not_investigated: T-LONG-FORM: no running-text region; the item is a single product composition with under 50 words.
T-FIVE-SECOND and T-RIVAL-NAME on interface labels: skipped, the item is an app component (Operate mode) with no hero; page title and navigation sit outside the capture frame.
T-READ-ALOUD: no brand voice supplied and too few sentences to hear a voice.
Async and after-action states: async.json was not captured, so no state copy after a click was read.
The capture shows only the first deploy row at a large scale; the 'Search speedup' and 'Pricing copy' rows were read from the DOM, not the tiles.
